title: Auto ring finder for limb joints: propose rings at girth minima and neck-into-wide-body transitions
description:
From the review of the user's 82-ring crawfish segmentation (2026-10-04, report rules R1-R5): 39 of the rings go around limbs. They are planar (slice perimeter about 1.02x the ring length); 25 sit at a local girth minimum; 25 sit where girth jumps 3x or more within one ring radius on one side and stays near 1x on the other (the user's 'neck coming into a wide object'); about 14 are true joints between similar podomeres at shallow 5-25% constrictions; ring lengths span 36x (0.012-0.44). Build a finder that proposes rings from these rules: sample girth along the limb skeleton (LimbAxis already exists) with plane slices, detect shallow minima (5% or more over plus or minus 0.5 r) and 3x one-sided jumps, and offer each as a candidate ring the user accepts or rejects in the ring tool. Plate (patch) rings are out of scope here; they need curvature valleys or the cross field (CRAW-31, PATCH-122). Evaluate against the user's rings: recall and precision of proposed rings vs the 39 limb rings in fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (a proposal matches when its plane slice lies within a set distance and angle of a user ring). Earlier ring_candidates (skeleton branch necks) was frozen and removed from the tool because candidates landed in the wrong places; this ticket must beat that measurably before anything is shown to the user.

Connection tool (CRAW-50, 2026-10-07): its neck is the globally narrowest plane slice along the path between two picks, so where a pick sits on a tapering part (leg tip, antenna) the slice next to the pick wins and the neck drifts toward it: 7 of 25 joint tests (rings ring_00, 03, 04, 07, 23, 31, 32 picked on either side) missed the joint this way. The girth rules here (local minimum against the surface plus or minus 0.5 r on both sides, one-sided 3x jump) are the right neck test there too; the connection tool should use the same rule rather than the global minimum, so both find necks one way. Not fixed by CRAW-31 (field-mode segments change a ring's shape between anchors, not where the neck is chosen).
definition-of-done:
1. Finder runs on the full crawfish in seconds. 2. Recall and precision against the user's 39 limb rings are on the ticket, with the matching criterion stated; target agreed with the user before UI work. 3. Candidates appear in the ring tool as accept/reject proposals only after the target is met.

4. The connection tool chooses its neck with this ticket's girth rules instead of the global minimum along the path, with the shared code in one place; picking either side of each of the 25 joints from the CRAW-50 sweep puts the neck at the joint (recall reported, the 7 previous misses listed individually).
testing-plan: 1. Offline benchmark comparing proposals to fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl limb rings. 2. Screenshots of proposals vs user rings.
changes-made: Measurement first, finder and connection-tool rule built, target NOT met; stopped before UI (DoD 2) for the user to agree a target. Shared neck rules live only in SurfaceConnection.connect: the path's girth profile is now adaptive (48 even samples, then every gap wider than a quarter of the narrower end's radius halved, at most 400), each sample flagged GIRTH_MINIMUM (narrowest within 0.5 r, both sides >=1.1x there) or SHOULDER (one side >=2x within 1.5 r, other side <=1.25x), and the connection tool's neck is the flagged sample the surface widens away from most (no longer the global narrowest). Thresholds differ from the ticket's 5%/3x/1r: our tangent-plane slices see joint jumps of 2-2.5x, and 5%/3x found the joint on 8 of 25 offline vs 16 with these. The Dijkstra stops at the end face and resumes for a repeated start (SurfaceConnection.spread). New LimbRingFinder: limbs are branches of the shortest-path tree from the surface's middle to its far tips (the voxel skeleton finds only 15 branches on the crawfish), each limb's profile run through connect, every flagged neck a proposal (deduplicated, snapped, as RingCandidates). Benchmark LimbRingFinderBenchmark (mvn test -Dtest=LimbRingFinderBenchmark): limb ring = user ring <=0.45 long whose plane slice is within 35% of its length (38 of 82); a proposal matches when its slice centroid is within one ring radius of the ring centroid and normals within 30 degrees. Results on the full crawfish (938k faces): finder recall 21/38 = 0.55, precision 23/130 = 0.18, 59 s (323 limbs; with 5% limb threshold 1400 limbs, recall 26/38, precision 37/280, 218 s), so DoD 1 (seconds) also fails; frozen ring_candidates recall 2/38, precision 2/4, 28 s. Connection sweep (picks 3 ring radii either side of each of the 25 joints along the ring normal; hit = snapped neck centroid within one ring radius): 11/25; of the 7 earlier misses ring_03 and ring_07 now hit, ring_00, 04, 23, 31, 32 still miss; earlier hits 05, 06, 11, 30, 36, 38, 40, 41, 42 miss with these picks (the old rule on the same refined profiles, by sample plane distance: 13/25 vs 16/25 for the new). Tests: SurfaceConnectionTest, SurfacePickerTest, Ring*Test green (52).

Second pass (data-driven, in progress, interim): LimbRingFinder rewritten: one candidate per groove band = the plane cut across the groove (normal = SurfaceCreases.acrossGroove) at the strongest uncovered groove vertex (strength >= 0.5), 6 features (groove fraction of the cut, mean valley strength, groove alignment, log girth ratio of narrow/wide side 1 r away, log length/diagonal), logistic weights fitted in LimbRingFinderBenchmark leave-one-model-out over IMG_4109 (fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl), IMG_4110, IMG_4111 (tmp copy cut before ring_51), dedupe best-first within 1 r / 30 deg. First held-out run: precision 0.60/0.47/0.36, recall 12/38=0.32, 7/41=0.17, 9/21=0.43; creases 2.3-3.9 s + finder 2.0-4.0 s per model. Ceiling: candidates (before scoring) touch only 20/38, 18/41, 10/21 limb rings, about half of them the non-groove (planar) ones, so candidate generation is the bottleneck.

Pass 2b, connection sweep on FIXED picks (2 and 3 ring radii either side of each of the 25 joints along the ring normal, 50 pairs, saved to tmp/joint_sweep_picks.tsv and reused for both runs; hit = snapped neck centroid within one ring radius): new neck rule 27/50, master's global-minimum rule 23/50 (same picks, master's SurfaceConnection swapped in). New hits master misses: ring_07 x2, ring_34@3, ring_37 x2, ring_44 x2; master hits new misses: ring_18@2, ring_36@3, ring_38@3. Keeping the new rule. Run-4 interim (plane refit around each groove band, 2 rounds): candidate ceiling 24/38, 24/41, 14/21 but held-out precision 0.30/0.15/0.31, recall 0.21/0.34/0.33 and finder 30-64 s, so the refit is being replaced.

Pass 2b run-6: refit removed; neck rules moved into one static SurfaceConnection.markNecks(along, girth, count, neck, rise) that connect and LimbRingFinder both call (public sample* arrays of SurfaceConnection made locals; spread() inlined into connect). Finder adds a girth-profile march from every groove cut (planes 0.25 r apart along the limb, axis turned toward the centroid drift, up to 4 r each side) and every markNecks neck on it is a candidate; 8 features (adds log neck rise, groove-cut flag; girth ratios now read off the profile). Ceiling 21/38, 19/41, 12/21 (groove cuts alone 19, 18, 9; before 20, 18, 10): the march adds little. Held-out precision 0.31/0.33/0.34, recall 11/38=0.29, 4/41=0.10, 10/21=0.48; finder 1.1-2.1 s + creases 2.3 s. Most misses sit within ~1 r of a candidate but tilted 30-80 deg, so the plane orientation, not position, is the main loss.

Pass 2b run-7: each groove band also cut by the shortest girdling plane (GirdlingPlane, seeded with the across direction) through the same seed, which gets its own profile march. Ceiling 23/38, 23/41, 14/21 (60/100 vs 50/100 for groove cuts alone; per kind across 19/18/9, girdling 10/17/9, profile necks 14/17/13). Held-out precision 0.29/0.33/0.19, recall 15/38=0.39, 9/41=0.22, 9/21=0.43; finder 1.5-2.1 s, creases 2.1-2.6 s.
